// purpose: @debuggen/model-provider - the compiler project for the monorepo typecheck gate. `pnpm typecheck` (= `pnpm demo:generate && tsc -b`) builds the root solution file, which lists this project after packages/shared because that is the only workspace this one sits on top of (AAP 0.2.2): the model boundary depends on @debuggen/shared and on nothing else in the repository, so the `references` array at the bottom of this file has exactly one entry.
// inherited: Everything that is not stated below is inherited from tsconfig.base.json and must stay that way - in particular `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, the no-unused/no-implicit diagnostics, `target`/`lib` ES2023, and the declaration-emit settings (`declaration`, `declarationMap`, `sourceMap`, `emitDeclarationOnly`, `incremental`). `noEmit` must never be added: TypeScript 6.0.3 rejects a referenced project that disables emit with TS6310 and the whole gate fails.
// format: Strict JSON, like tsconfig.base.json, the root tsconfig.json and every other tsconfig in this repository: both a JSONC-aware reader (`ts.readConfigFile`) and a bare `JSON.parse` can read it, so no consumer has to know which one to reach for. tsc, ESLint, Vitest, tsup and Prettier would all accept comments in a tsconfig file, but the rationale is recorded in the `"// …"` string keys of this object instead so that every reader gets it. TypeScript ignores unknown TOP-LEVEL keys, which is what makes the convention safe; a `"// …"` key inside `compilerOptions` is a hard error instead (TS5023, "Unknown compiler option"), so every note about a single option lives up here under a `"// compilerOptions.<option>"` key and never beside the option itself.
// compilerOptions.composite: Already true in the base; restated because the root solution file references this project and a non-composite reference fails `tsc -b` outright (TS6306). Keeping it local means a future edit to the base cannot silently break the gate at this project. tsup is the other consumer of this file (`tsconfig: './tsconfig.json'` in tsup.config.ts). If its `.d.ts` step ever objects to `composite` / `incremental`, the override belongs in that file's `dts.compilerOptions` - never here, because dropping `composite` breaks the solution build.
// compilerOptions.module: The base defaults to "ESNext" + "bundler" for the bundled/web workspaces and instructs Node-targeted projects to override with NodeNext. This package is Node-only: apps/local-service loads it in the service process, apps/vscode-extension bundles it into the VSIX for the same process, and src/prompt-loader.ts reads the versioned prompt files under apps/local-service/prompts/** with `node:fs` / `node:path`. Nothing here runs in a page, so the project is type-checked under real Node ESM resolution instead of a bundler approximation (AAP 0.3.4). Consequence for every source file in src/**: relative specifiers must carry an explicit ".js" extension (`export * from "./provider.js"`, `import { … } from "./providers/anthropic.js"`, `import { … } from "./deterministic/rules.js"`), and directory specifiers must name the file (`"./providers/index.js"`). Extensionless relative imports are a compile error here by design - they would break real Node consumers of dist/index.js. tsup/esbuild resolve a "./x.js" specifier from a TypeScript importer back to "./x.ts", so the bundle is unaffected.
// compilerOptions.rootDir: Per-workspace (the base deliberately leaves it unset), so the declaration tree under .tsbuild/ mirrors src/ exactly: src/index.ts -> .tsbuild/index.d.ts and src/providers/anthropic.ts -> .tsbuild/providers/anthropic.d.ts, matching the single "." path the package.json `exports` map advertises under dist/.
// compilerOptions.types: The base sets no `types` so that one workspace's ambient globals cannot bleed into another. This package needs exactly one: @types/node 24.13.6 (a root devDependency, resolved through the workspace-root node_modules/@types by the ancestor walk-up, which is why it is absent from this package's manifest). It types the `node:fs` / `node:path` / `node:url` builtins behind src/prompt-loader.ts and the `process.env` reads behind src/factory.ts (DEBUGGEN_PROVIDER, DEBUGGEN_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Deliberately no "lib": ["DOM"] override and no "chrome"/"vscode" entry: a model call never happens in a page, and @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.127.0 ships its own fetch typings, so the Node lib set is sufficient.
// compilerOptions.outDir: NOT overridden: "outDir" / "declarationDir" / "tsBuildInfoFile". The base already anchors them per project with `${configDir}`, which resolves to the directory of THIS file, so declarations and the incremental stamp land in packages/model-provider/.tsbuild (ignored by .gitignore and .prettierignore). tsc must never write into packages/model-provider/dist: that directory belongs to tsup and holds the artefacts the `exports` map points at.
// compilerOptions.skipLibCheck: NOT overridden (the base already enables it) and no strictness flag is relaxed or added on top of the base.
// include: src/** only, and deliberately including the colocated `*.test.ts` files - src/structured.test.ts, src/prompt-loader.test.ts, src/redact-guard.test.ts, src/providers/deterministic.test.ts and src/providers/anthropic.test.ts - so the typecheck gate and ESLint's type-aware project service cover the tests too. They import `{ describe, it, expect, vi }` from "vitest" explicitly rather than relying on globals, and vitest resolves from the workspace-root node_modules, so no "vitest/globals" entry is needed in `types`. Tests never reach dist/: tsup bundles only what src/index.ts imports.
// exclude: Replaces the base's inherited list; resolved relative to this directory, so it means packages/model-provider/dist, /.tsbuild and /node_modules. Belt and braces: `include` already restricts the input set to src/**, and the tsup output in dist/ plus the declaration output in .tsbuild/ sit outside it.
// references: The one substantive difference from packages/shared/tsconfig.json, which has no references: this project consumes @debuggen/shared (ids, Result, SourceLocation, the logger and DebuggenError), so `tsc -b` must build that project first. No other reference may be added. @debuggen/panel-schema, @debuggen/instrumentation, @debuggen/telemetry and @debuggen/protocol are deliberately not dependencies of the model boundary (AAP 0.2.2): callers pass their own Zod authoring schema and their deterministic normaliser in, so this package stays ignorant of plans, panels, events and messages. eslint.config.js fails the build on an import of any of them, and a reference to @debuggen/protocol would close a cycle, since protocol sits above this layer.
